title: Revelation Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Revelation chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Revelation Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Revelation Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did the four angels hold in Revelation 7:1?
options: The four winds of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: The four winds of the earth
questions.explanation: The verse states that the four angels were holding the four winds of the earth, preventing them from blowing on the earth, sea, or trees.

questions.question: From which direction did the other angel ascend in Revelation 7:2?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that another angel ascended from the east, indicating the direction.

questions.question: How many servants of God were sealed according to Revelation 7:4?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.

questions.question: Of the tribe of Juda, how many were sealed?
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:5 states that of the tribe of Juda, twelve thousand were sealed.

questions.question: True or False: The angel in Revelation 7:2 had the seal of the living God.
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the angel ascending from the east had the seal of the living God.

questions.question: How many tribes of Israel had twelve thousand sealed from them according to Revelation 7:6?
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:6 lists six tribes of Israel, each with twelve thousand sealed.

questions.question: True or False: The wind was allowed to blow on the earth in Revelation 7:3.
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:3 states that the angels were instructed to hurt not the earth, the sea, nor the trees until the servants of God were sealed.

questions.question: What was commanded by the angel in Revelation 7:3?
questions.explanation: The angel commanded not to hurt the earth, the sea, nor the trees until the sealing was done.

questions.question: True or False: The number of the sealed is mentioned in Revelation 7:4.
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:4 explicitly states the number of those who were sealed, which is one hundred and forty-four thousand.

questions.question: What comes first in the events of Revelation 7?
options: The cry of the angel from the east
The angels holding back the winds
questions.correctAnswer: The angels holding back the winds
questions.explanation: The first event described is the vision of the four angels standing on the four corners of the earth holding the winds.

questions.question: How many tribes of the children of Israel are mentioned in Revelation 7?
questions.explanation: Twelve tribes of the children of Israel are mentioned as being sealed in Revelation 7.

medium.title: Revelation Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Revelation Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How many tribes of Israel had twelve thousand sealed from each tribe according to Revelation 7?
questions.explanation: The text mentions twelve tribes of Israel that were sealed with twelve thousand from each: Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph, and Benjamin (Revelation 7:5-8).

questions.question: What did the great multitude hold in their hands as they stood before the throne?
questions.explanation: The great multitude was described as being clothed with white robes and holding palms in their hands (Revelation 7:9).

questions.question: True or False: The angels worshipped God by falling on their faces before the throne.
questions.explanation: The angels, along with the elders and the four beasts, fell before the throne on their faces and worshipped God (Revelation 7:11).

questions.question: What is promised to those who serve before the throne of God, according to Revelation 7?
options: They shall not hunger nor thirst
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not hunger nor thirst
questions.explanation: The passage states that they shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more, and God shall provide for them (Revelation 7:16-17).

questions.question: How does Revelation 7:10 emphasize the importance of salvation?
options: By directing praise to God and the Lamb
By detailing the nature of sin
questions.correctAnswer: By directing praise to God and the Lamb
questions.explanation: The multitude cried with a loud voice, saying, 'Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb' (Revelation 7:10), emphasizing that salvation is worthy of praise.

questions.question: True or False: The elders in Revelation 7 ask about the identity of those in white robes.
questions.explanation: One of the elders indeed asks John about those arrayed in white robes and their origin (Revelation 7:13).

questions.question: What does Revelation 7:14 say about the robes of those who came out of great tribulation?
options: They are made white in the blood of the Lamb
questions.correctAnswer: They are made white in the blood of the Lamb
questions.explanation: The verse explains that these individuals have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 7:14).

questions.question: According to Revelation 7:12, what attributes are ascribed to God?
questions.explanation: The angels declare blessings, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honour, power, and might to God (Revelation 7:12), highlighting His attributes.

questions.question: How many were sealed from the tribe of Levi?
questions.explanation: The text states that twelve thousand were sealed from the tribe of Levi (Revelation 7:7).

questions.question: What is the significance of the winds being held back by the angels in Revelation 7:1?
questions.explanation: The angels holding back the winds signifies God's control over the earth and His timing for judgment and protection (Revelation 7:1).

questions.question: True or False: The chapter indicates that the multitude in heaven is limited to a specific nation.
questions.explanation: The great multitude is described as coming from all nations, kindreds, and tongues, indicating inclusivity (Revelation 7:9).

questions.question: What does Revelation 7:15 say about the relationship of the sealed ones with God?
options: They will serve God day and night
They will be distant from God
questions.correctAnswer: They will serve God day and night
questions.explanation: The verse states that they shall serve Him day and night in His temple, demonstrating their close relationship with God (Revelation 7:15).

hard.title: Revelation Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Revelation Chapter 7.

questions.question: What is the total number of those sealed from all the tribes of the children of Israel?
questions.explanation: The total number sealed is mentioned in Revelation 7:4 as 'an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.'

questions.question: Which tribe is mentioned first among those sealed in Revelation 7?
questions.explanation: The tribe of Juda is listed first in Revelation 7:5: 'Of the tribe of Juda were sealed twelve thousand.'

questions.question: What did the multitude in white robes cry out before the throne?
questions.explanation: In Revelation 7:10, the multitude cries, 'Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.'

questions.question: According to Revelation 7:14, how did the multitude in white robes make their robes white?
options: In the blood of the Lamb
questions.correctAnswer: In the blood of the Lamb
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:14 states that they 'have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.'

questions.question: What does Revelation 7:16 say about the needs of the multitude before the throne?
options: They will work for their food
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:16 states, 'They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.'

questions.question: True or False: The Lamb is said to lead the multitude to living fountains of waters.
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:17 states, 'For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters.'

questions.question: What is a significant theme of the multitude in Revelation 7 that echoes the Beatitudes in Matthew 5?
questions.explanation: The multitude who came out of great tribulation are comforted, akin to the Beatitude in Matthew 5:4, 'Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.'

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Revelation 7:10, where the multitude ascribes salvation to both God and the Lamb?
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:10 employs parallelism as it repeats the structure 'to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.'

questions.question: True or False: The elders in Revelation 7 ask John about the multitude in white robes after they have already praised God.
questions.explanation: The elders ask John about the multitude in Revelation 7:13 after the multitude has already praised God, indicating a sequence of events.

questions.question: How does Revelation 7:15 describe the role of the multitude before the throne of God?
options: They shall serve Him day and night
questions.correctAnswer: They shall serve Him day and night
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:15 says, 'Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple.'

questions.question: What Old Testament imagery is reflected in the description of the Lamb feeding and leading the multitude in Revelation 7:17?
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:17 reflects the imagery of the Lord as a shepherd, akin to Psalm 23:1, 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.'

questions.question: What is the significance of the number 12,000 in Revelation 7:5-8 with respect to the tribes?
options: A multiple of the twelve tribes
questions.correctAnswer: A multiple of the twelve tribes
questions.explanation: The number 12,000 indicates a perfect number associated with the twelve tribes of Israel, as seen in Revelation 7:5-8.

questions.question: Which Greek word used in Revelation 7:14 for 'tribulation' suggests a period of severe trial?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'Thlipsis' used in Revelation 7:14 denotes a severe trial or affliction, highlighting the suffering endured before salvation.

theological.title: Revelation Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Revelation Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the number of those sealed from the tribes of Israel?
questions.explanation: The number of them which were sealed is specifically stated as one hundred and forty and four thousand in Revelation 7:4.

questions.question: Which tribe does NOT have twelve thousand sealed according to Revelation 7?
questions.explanation: Ephraim is not mentioned in the sealing list; instead, Joseph is listed along with his other tribes in Revelation 7:5-8.

questions.question: What did the great multitude in white robes hold in their hands?
questions.explanation: The great multitude stood before the throne with palms in their hands as stated in Revelation 7:9.

questions.question: What does the multitude cry out in Revelation 7:10?
options: Praise be to the Most High
questions.explanation: The multitude cries, 'Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb,' as recorded in Revelation 7:10.

questions.question: What has the multitude done to their robes?
questions.explanation: The multitude has washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb, as noted in Revelation 7:14.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by His act of wiping away tears?
questions.explanation: God wiping away all tears from their eyes illustrates His mercy and compassion towards His people, as seen in Revelation 7:17.

questions.question: What does Revelation 7 teach about God's protection?
options: God will protect only the mighty
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes that God seals His servants in their foreheads to protect them from harm, as stated in Revelation 7:3.

questions.question: How does Revelation 7 connect to the broader narrative of Scripture regarding God's people?
options: God's people will always be few
God's people will face no trials
questions.explanation: The sealing of the 144,000 illustrates God's eternal security for His chosen people throughout the tribulation, connecting to the broader theme of redemption and preservation.

questions.question: What do the four angels represent in Revelation 7:1?
questions.explanation: The four angels holding back the winds symbolize God's protection over the earth and His people until they are sealed, as indicated in Revelation 7:1.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'great tribulation' in Revelation 7:14 imply about the experiences of the multitude?
questions.explanation: The multitude came out of great tribulation, indicating they endured significant suffering for their faith, as stated in Revelation 7:14.

questions.question: What aspect of worship is emphasized in Revelation 7:11?
questions.explanation: The angels and elders worshipped God by falling on their faces and proclaiming loudly, emphasizing the reverence and intensity of worship in Revelation 7:11.

questions.question: What does the sealing of the 144,000 demonstrate about God's sovereignty?
questions.explanation: The sealing indicates God's sovereign control over who is protected and preserved during the tribulation, as shown in Revelation 7:3.

questions.question: What two attributes of God are reflected in the blessings proclaimed in Revelation 7:12?
questions.explanation: The blessings in Revelation 7:12 reflect God's attributes of glory and honor, emphasizing His supreme worthiness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care for humanity during suffering. What does Revelation 7:16-17 actually teach?
options: God is unconcerned with earthly matters
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:16-17 teaches that God will care for His people, providing comfort and sustenance, thus showing His concern for humanity during suffering.

questions.question: What does the act of crying out for salvation signify about the multitude's understanding of their needs?
options: They acknowledged their need for God
They were unaware of their plight
questions.correctAnswer: They acknowledged their need for God
questions.explanation: The multitude's cry for salvation signifies their recognition of their dependence on God for deliverance, as expressed in Revelation 7:10.
